q-160790.problem: What is the value of $f(t)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t+3} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(t+3) \\ \sqrt{{t}^{2}-1}\end{aligned}]$ at $t=-2?$
q-160790.worked_solution:
To evaluate, we substitute $t=-2$ into the function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{(-2)+3} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡((-2)+3) \\ \sqrt{(-2)^{2}-1}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{1} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡1 \\ \sqrt{4-1}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So the value of $f(t)$ at $t=-2$ is the vector $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}].$

q-75001.name: Question 13
q-75001.worked_solution:
Evaluating the function at $t=\frac{\pi }{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}),\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}),\,6⟩ \\  & =⟨2\cdot \frac{1}{2},\,4\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,6⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2\sqrt{3},\,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the magnitude of this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|r(\frac{\pi }{3})| & =\sqrt{{(1)}^{2}+{(2\sqrt{3})}^{2}+(6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+12+36} \\  & =\sqrt{49} \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$
